text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages with eight quote variants each, for testing citation checking.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Kelora Valley Water and Sanitation Project found that 14 of the planned 20 boreholes were operational by March 2023. Water committees in Ndavi and Rusoto districts collect a monthly fee of two hundred shillings per household, and 68% of households reported paying on time. Latrine coverage rose from 31% to 57% across the target villages. However, the evaluation team did not find evidence that handwashing stations were maintained after the first dry season. Several committees had no spare parts for hand pumps, and repairs often took more than three weeks. The team recommends that the project train local mechanics before the final year begins.

variants.paraphrase: Evaluators saw no proof that handwashing stations were kept up once the first dry season had passed.

passages.source_passage: Before each session, trainers should remind volunteers that the Sandmere Coast Early Warning Network relies on them to relay alerts within 15 minutes of receiving a message. Each volunteer covers roughly forty households, so a team of six can reach most of a fishing village before the tide turns. Do not wait for a second confirmation from the district office; the first siren is enough. Volunteers must never send families back to collect livestock once an evacuation has begun. During the 2021 drill, 83% of households reached the Brackwater school shelter in under an hour, but older residents often needed help. Pair each new volunteer with an experienced one for at least two drills, and record attendance on the yellow sheet.

passages.source_passage: Board members will be pleased to learn that the Puente Alto Scholarship Fund supported 212 girls in secondary school during the 2023 academic year. Retention reached 91%, up from 84% the previous year, largely because mentors visited families in the Valle Seco region each term. Twelve scholars sat the national examination and nine passed with distinction. Not every result was positive, however. Transport stipends did not keep pace with fuel prices, and some girls in remote hamlets missed classes during the rainy months. The programme team hasn't yet secured funding to extend bus routes, and asks the board to approve a reallocation of $18,000 from the contingency line at the June meeting.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2024, the Harbourline Community Counselling Service held 1,140 individual sessions and 36 group sessions across its four drop-in centres. Clients completed a short wellbeing questionnaire at intake and again after six sessions; average scores improved by 22%. Referrals from the Eastmoor primary health clinic rose sharply after counsellors began attending its weekly staff meetings. No client was turned away for inability to pay. However, waiting times did not fall as planned, and the Fennick Road centre still had a backlog of almost three weeks by September. Two counsellors left during the quarter and were not replaced, which placed additional strain on remaining staff. Supervision sessions continued fortnightly.

passages.source_passage: The Ombasa Farmer Field School Network now operates 48 schools in the Lower Teru basin, up from 30 at the start of 2022. Each school meets weekly through the growing season, and facilitators are themselves farmers who graduated from an earlier cohort. Participants who adopted mulching and intercropping reported maize yields roughly 35% higher than neighbouring plots. Seed fairs held in April drew more than nine hundred visitors. The board should note that the drought-tolerant sorghum trial did not perform as expected; germination was poor and no plots reached harvest in the western cluster. Management doesn't recommend expanding the trial until soil testing is complete, and will present revised plans in October.

passages.source_passage: Since January 2023, the Kibwezi-Lunda District Health Programme has trained 260 community health workers, of whom 241 remain active. Each worker visits about seventy households a month, screening children for malnutrition and referring pregnant women to the Mafinga health centre. Facility deliveries in the catchment increased from 58% to 74% over eighteen months. Stock-outs remain a concern: workers did not receive oral rehydration salts for six weeks in the second quarter. We also learned that monthly stipends were never paid on time in two sub-counties, which contributed to most of the nineteen dropouts. The executive team proposes switching to mobile money payments and asks the board to endorse this change at its next sitting.

passages.source_passage: At the mid-point of the programme, the Tamarind Savings Initiative had formed 185 village savings and loan groups across Sefa and Odumase counties, against a target of 200. Women make up 79% of members. Average savings per member reached the equivalent of $46 by the end of the second cycle, and loan repayment rates exceeded 95% in most groups. Evaluators found that groups trained by community-based facilitators performed as well as those trained by staff. However, the planned link to the Odumase rural bank was not established, and members still couldn't access larger loans for livestock or equipment. No group reported losing its cash box, though record-keeping was weak where few members could read.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term review of the Lakeshore Nets for Life campaign covered distribution in Mbere and Kasanga districts between May and August 2023. Teams delivered 112,000 long-lasting insecticidal nets, roughly one net for every two residents. A household survey of 1,500 homes found that 71% of children under five had slept under a net the previous night. Hang-up visits clearly helped: usage was higher in villages where volunteers returned within a week. Yet the review did not find similar gains among pregnant women, and many nets in fishing camps were not used at all because residents slept outdoors. Distribution registers weren't reconciled with census data, so coverage estimates should be treated with caution.

passages.source_passage: When you accompany outreach nurses from the Sundari Clinic to villages around Pathgaon, your first task is to help register every pregnant woman you meet. Encourage each mother to attend at least four antenatal visits, and remind families that the clinic is open from 8 am to 4 pm six days a week. Never advise a mother to delay breastfeeding; newborns should be put to the breast within one hour of birth. In 2022, only 62% of births in our area were attended by a skilled provider, so your home visits matter. If a woman has heavy bleeding or a severe headache, do not wait for the next outreach day. Call the duty nurse immediately and stay with the family.

passages.source_passage: Youth unemployment in the Marrow Hills district stands at an estimated 38%, more than double the national average. The Copperline Vocational Training Centre was founded in 2016 to address this gap and has since graduated 1,420 young people in welding, tailoring, solar installation and catering. Tracer surveys show that 64% of graduates found paid work within six months. Demand for places is high, and last year the centre received nearly three applications for every available seat. However, our existing workshops were not designed for modern equipment, and the centre has no dedicated space for solar training. Many young women did not enrol in technical courses because there was no childcare on site. This proposal seeks to remove both barriers.
